o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish دوش (düş, “dream, vision”), from Proto-Turkic *tǖĺ (“dream”).
From Arabic عِلْمِيّ (ʕilmiyy). By surface analysis, elm + -i

From Proto-Turkic *čEkük, *čEküč (“hammer”). Cognate with Karakhanid [script needed] (čekük), [script needed] (čeküč), Turkish çekiç. A connection to the stem çək- ("to pull") has been proposed. May be related to Persian چکش (“čakoš”).
Borrowed from Russian империали́зм (imperialízm), from French impérialisme.
From Classical Persian خَرَابَه (xarāba), from Arabic خَرَابَة (ḵarāba).
